c.tagline: Sleepy Mekong capital of gilded stupas, baguettes, and river sunsets.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmetered; agree the fare (or use a fixed airport rate) before riding, or book through the Loca app for set pricing.

emergency.note: Fire: 190. English-speaking dispatch cannot be guaranteed; larger hotels can call on your behalf, and Mahosot Hospital / Alliance International Medical Center are common expat referrals.

avoid.reason: Motorbike bag-snatching and petty theft happen along the riverfront and quiet streets at night; agree tuk-tuk fares in advance.

hood_desc: The compact French-colonial core around the fountain plaza, packed with cafes, bakeries, and boutique hotels; ideal for first-time visitors who want to walk everywhere.
A breezy strip along Fa Ngum Road with sunset bars, the night market, and river views; best for travelers wanting evening atmosphere and riverside dining.
The grand ceremonial boulevard linking the Presidential Palace to the Patuxai monument, lined with government buildings and international-chain hotels; suits business travelers.
A quieter, more spiritual district anchored by the golden Pha That Luang stupa, with wide avenues and fewer tourists; good for those seeking a peaceful base near temples.
The bustling downtown market quarter near the bus terminal and Mekong bridge road, popular with budget travelers and those needing early transit connections.

water.note: Tap water isn't safe even in the capital; drink bottled or filtered water, though commercial ice in tourist spots is usually fine.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (Lao Kip) directly to the conductor on board; there is no rechargeable transit card. Intercity and airport shuttle buses are also cash-only, though some private minivan transfers can be prepaid online.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6am-6pm with limited frequency and no reliable night service; tuk-tuks, taxis, or the Loca app fill the gap in the evenings.
transit.note: Public transit is minimal for a capital city; most residents and visitors get around by tuk-tuk, taxi, rented scooter/bicycle, or the Loca ride-hailing app.

train: Thanaleng-Nong Khai cross-border train to Thailand
bus: Talat Sao Bus Station (local & northern routes)

tip.r: Not traditionally expected in Lao culture, but rounding up bills or leaving 5-10% at tourist-oriented restaurants, and tipping tour guides/drivers a few dollars per day, is appreciated.
